edge_cases: S=32 (single output crouton tile) but D=128 (deep head-dim reduction, accumulated over 4 K-tiles)

K is stored [S,D] row-major (row j IS key vector j) -- scores = Q.K^T needs no explicit transpose, only swapped tile indices in the crouton weight pack (unlike the AV sibling, where V is already B[K,N]-shaped)

the HVX baseline pays an EXTRA one-time transpose of K into a cacheable Kt[D,S] buffer (needed for its contiguous-row AXPY formulation) -- the HMX expert avoids this entirely by packing straight from K, giving it a bigger edge than the AV sibling's 1.22x
Q6_mxclracc_hf clears the persistent hf accumulator ONCE; 4 (activation,weight) load pairs accumulate into it before the single store
fp16 crouton layout off(r,c)=(r/2)*64+c*2+(r&1) for Q, weight, output, per D-tile
HVX/HMX qf16 arithmetic is non-IEEE -> tolerance compare, not bit-exact
D=128 is a deep reduction -> qf16 rounding drifts more (near-cancellation outputs close to zero); widened tolerance atol=8e-3/rtol=1.2e-2
crouton pack/unpack staged via cacheable buffers + bulk vector copy
missing-transpose near-miss (computes Q.K, not Q.K^T) must fail the tolerance gate
name: fp16_attention_qkt_hmx
